 Court No. - 65
 Hon'Ble Krishan Pahal, J. 
1. List has been revised.
2. Supplementary affidavit filed today is taken on record.

3. Heard Sri Ajay Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for applicant, Sri Shivakant, learned counsel for the informant, Sri Ram Mohit Yadav, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
4.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in Case Crime No.98 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station-Bindki, District-Fatehpur with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the FIR is delayed and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
Only one witness has been examined during trial, as such, there is no likelihood of early conclusion of trial.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is in jail since 17.04.2024, as such, applicant has been in incarceration for about more than one year and four months and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the informant and learned A.G.A. have vehemently opposed the bail application and placed reliance on the certified copy of the statement of P.W.2 who has been examined on 27.08.2025 and has nominated the applicant.
It is further argued that FIR is prompt and the deceased expired within the precincts of the house of the applicant, as such, applicant is not entitled for bail.
7. This Court had called for status of trial from the trial court concerned.
As per the status report dated 13.08.2025 received from the trial court concerned, two witnesses have been examined.

8. The Supreme Court in case of X Vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr., 2024 INSC 909, has held that once the trial has commenced, it should be allowed to reach to its final conclusion, which may either result in conviction or acquittal of the accused.

entities.text: X Vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr., 2024 INSC 909
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail should not be normally granted to the accused after the charge has been framed.
It should also not be granted by looking into the discrepancies here or there in the deposition.

9. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the fact that two witnesses have already been examined, FIR being prompt coupled with the fact that deceased expired within the precincts of the house of the applicant, I do not find it a fit case for grant of bail to Arjun vs State Of U.P. on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178136631/
2 the applicant.
10. The bail application is found devoid of merits and is, accordingly, rejected.

11. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously in view of the principle as has been laid down in the recent judgments of the Supreme Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab; 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India; (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.
